response: {"text":"A group of ten researchers gathered to discuss ways to speed up the description and classification of stone tools. Rather than trying to create a full classification system, they concentrated on clearly defining the observable features of each piece, aiming for a method that could be applied across an entire continent instead of just a local area. They examined various types of paper data cards and the computer hardware needed to handle them. The team produced a list of precise definitions for each feature and designed a standardized worksheet for recording information about the artifacts. These worksheets were organized so the data could be easily transferred onto common data cards for analysis, with the goal of spotting meaningful groupings of characteristics. By using the worksheets in trial studies of regional collections, they plan to identify needed refinements and assess how practical fast‑processing techniques are for this kind of typological work."}
